_README: The register of parish ministries. `npm run ministries` renders it into the card grid on ministries.html and into the body of each ministry's own page, and regenerates MINISTRIES-FOR-THE-PARISH.md. This file is the ONE place a ministry's description, team and status live: the card and the page are stamped from the same entry, so they cannot disagree. Add a ministry by adding an entry here — never by writing a card into the markup.
_rules: A PERSON RENDERS ONLY WITH BOTH `source` AND `permission`. `source` says where the pairing between this person and this ministry came from; `permission` names the recorded approval that allows publishing the name at all. Missing either is a build error, not a silent omission. See data/parish-facts.json → _rosterPermission, which is what `permission: "_rosterPermission"` refers to.

TITLES ARE NOT INVENTED. `role` may only carry a title the source actually gives. The parish newsletter gives an explicit title to Dr. Judy Marrs (Director) and to the Parish Council and Philoptochos officers, and to nobody else — everywhere else it prints an organisation heading and a bare name. `role: null` renders the bare name. Nobody becomes a director, chair, coordinator or lead who was not called one in the source.

A `photos` ENTRY IS A HINT, NOT A FILE. It describes what a photograph would show, and renders an empty placeholder frame. The Parish Council's roster approval covers no photograph — see _rosterPermission item (3) — so if an entry ever gains a `file`, the build refuses it until a `permission` sits beside it.

ONE MINISTRY, ONE PAGE. Two entries claiming the same `page` is an error. The Philoptochos board lives on ministry-philoptochos.html and nowhere else; the Parish Council roster lives on about.html and nowhere else, which is why the Council's page links rather than restates.

`status` is one of: awaiting (nothing beyond the one-line description), partial (some of it is sourced, some is not), current (the ministry has supplied its content). A page says which, in as many words, on its face. `current` with nothing to show is an error.
`needs` is what the ministry would have to supply for the entry to move on. It is NOT shown on the website — it is what MINISTRIES-FOR-THE-PARISH.md is built from.

CONTACT DETAILS ARE NOT REPEATED HERE. The office address, telephone number and hours come from data/site.json → contact at build time. `involve.askFor` may only name somebody who already appears in this entry's `team`.

awaiting.label: Content needed from the ministry
awaiting.note: Nothing beyond the description above has been supplied yet. Ask at coffee hour or write to the parish office in the meantime.

partial.label: Some detail still to come
partial.note: What is here is sourced. The rest is waiting on the ministry itself.

involveIntro: This ministry welcomes newcomers, and does not require you to have been here long. Ask at coffee hour, or write to the parish office and it will be passed on.
noTeamNote: The parish has not published who leads this ministry. The parish office will know, and will pass a message on.
noPersonalContact: No personal email address or telephone number is published here: write to the parish office and it will be passed on.

ministries.title: Parish Council
ministries.card: Elected stewards responsible for the temporal affairs of the parish, serving alongside the presiding priest.
ministries.cardSource: data/parish-facts.json → parishCouncil; the live parish site's /parish-ministries/ page.
ministries.teamNote: The Council roster is published in one place only — on the About page — so that a correction has one page to reach. The committees each member leads are on the Parish Council Committees page.

involve.intro: The Parish Council is elected by the stewards of the parish, so unlike the other ministries here it is not one you join by volunteering. How a steward stands for election, and when elections are held, is among what this page is still waiting on. Council members are parishioners rather than staff, and are glad to be asked questions in the meantime.

What each committee does, and who leads it

ministries.needs: How a steward stands for election, and when elections are held; what a Council member is committing to in hours; whether meetings are open to stewards. The roster itself is not needed here — it is on the About page and stays there.

ministries.title: Choir
ministries.card: Those who sing in the divine services.
ministries.cardSource: The parish newsletter lists CHOIR as a parish organisation, which is what settles that one exists — the live parish site has no page for it. No officer is named.
ministries.needs: Who directs the choir; when it rehearses; whether a singer needs to read music or Byzantine notation, and whether Greek is needed; how somebody joins. Separately: whether the parish has chanters distinct from the choir — the newsletter says nothing about chanters and an earlier draft of this site invented a combined 'Choir & Chanters', so the question is open rather than settled.
